title: Turán density of K_4^- (the 2/7 conjecture)
premise_risks: Upper bound quoted to 4 decimals (0.28689 in Falgas-Ravry-Vaughan)
plain: Take a collection of triples from n points such that no 4 points carry 3 or more of their 4 triples. How large a fraction of all triples can you take? A recursive construction gets 2/7 and computer-aided proofs show you can't beat about 0.2868. Prove 2/7 is right, or beat it.
math: Let $K_4^-$ be the $3$-graph on 4 vertices with 3 edges and $\pi(K_4^-)=\lim_n \mathrm{ex}(n,K_4^-)/\binom n3$. Known: $2/7\le \pi(K_4^-)\le 0.2868$. Prove $\pi(K_4^-)=2/7$ (Frankl-Furedi/Mubayi conjecture), or improve the upper bound.
review_note: Known: Lower 2/7: Frankl-Furedi (1984) recursive construction. Upper: Baber-Talbot about 0.2871; Falgas-Ravry-Vaughan, 'Applications of the semi-definite method to the Turán density problem for 3-graphs', Combin. Probab. Comput. 22 (2013): about 0.2868. The density is stated as still unknown in Falgas-Ravry-Pikhurko-Vaughan-Volec, J. London Math. Soc. (2023). The codegree threshold of K_4^- is solved (arXiv:2112.09396).
